item.title: His Phone Revealed What Happened To The 98 Year Old
item.description: In 2018, 17-year-old Gavon Ramsay broke into his 98-year-old neighbor Margaret Douglas’s Ohio home and killed her. Investigators later recovered video evidence from Ramsay’s phone, leading to his conviction and a life sentence without parole.

item.title: 50 Cent Has Been Calling Out Diddy For Years
item.description: 50 Cent and Sean “Diddy” Combs have feuded publicly for nearly two decades, with 50 repeatedly criticizing Combs and distancing himself from him. Their rivalry intensified as Combs faced legal scrutiny, leading 50 Cent to produce a Netflix documentary about his career and allegations.

item.title: Her Death Was Ruled Homicide Then Changed To Suicide
item.description: Ellen Greenberg was found dead in her Philadelphia apartment in 2011 with 20 stab wounds. Her death was initially ruled a homicide before being changed to suicide. A 2025 review upheld the suicide ruling, while federal prosecutors later sought records related to how the case was handled.

item.title: She Was Failed By The Adults Who Should Have Protected Her
item.description: Lisa Plumb has spoken publicly about enduring childhood sexual abuse from multiple adults in her family and community. She later became a licensed marriage and family therapist, using her experiences to advocate for survivors and stronger protections for children.

item.title: How Magnus Carlsen Became Chess’s Greatest Rival
item.description: Magnus Carlsen became a chess grandmaster at 13 and went on to dominate the game for more than a decade. He won the World Chess Championship in 2013 and built a reputation for exceptional endgame play, consistency and an ability to outlast the world’s strongest opponents.

item.title: The Murder Verdict That Was Changed To Manslaughter
item.description: Louise Woodward was convicted of second-degree murder after eight-month-old Matthew Eappen died from severe head injuries in 1997. A judge later reduced the conviction to involuntary manslaughter and sentenced her to time served, a decision upheld 4–3 by Massachusetts’ highest court.

item.title: She Lured Her Fiancé’s Lover Into A Deadly Ambush
item.description: After Antonetta Stevens discovered her fiancé was having an affair with Ashley Bocanegra, investigators said she and her sister-in-law lured Ashley to a Georgia apartment complex. The two women then attacked her, and Ashley later died from her injuries.
